clue.text: Harry Potter author has no stomach for arguing

indicators.note: the stomach is the middle of the body, so the central letter of the author's name is dropped

parts.note: J K Rowling wrote the Harry Potter books

explanation.surface: A jibe that the Harry Potter author lacks the appetite for a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has no stomach' removes the middle letter, L, of the seven-letter surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowing (rhyming with 'cowing') is British informal for quarrelling noisily.

clue.text: Spinster is game

explanation.surface: A dated word for an unmarried woman, offered as a card game.
explanation.definitionFit: An unmarried older woman was once so called, and it is also a children's card game where you avoid holding the odd queen.

clue.text: Out of work, one on state benefit with nothing to lose

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: to lose says the following nothing must be taken out of the benefit word

parts.note: the dole is British slang for unemployment benefit
nothing is the figure zero, O

explanation.surface: Someone unemployed and on benefits has nothing to lose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with nothing to lose' reads as resignation, but 'nothing' is the zero letter and 'to lose' signals its removal.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle can mean not employed, with no work to do.

clue.text: Advice fellow heard at social event

indicators.note: heard says the word for fellow is to be taken by its sound

parts.note: a fellow is a guy
a dance is a social event

explanation.surface: Seeking counsel from a man you overheard at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Guidance is counsel or direction, the same as advice.

clue.text: Cylinder movin 'up and down

explanation.surface: A spool that jiggles about.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped G is shown by the apostrophe: 'movin' up and down' is bobbin', i.e. bobbing with the G clipped off as in casual speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A bobbin is a reel or spool for thread, and bobbing means rising and falling, here clipped in speech.

clue.text: Female supporter seen round goal

indicators.note: round means the supporter's letters go around the goal

parts.note: a bra is an undergarment that supports
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A woman fan spotted near the goalmouth at a football match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporter' and 'goal' suggest football, but the supporter is an undergarment and the goal is an aim.
explanation.definitionFit: Brenda is a woman's name, so it stands for a female in crossword style.

clue.text: Frivolous person, some kind of nut

explanation.surface: Calling a flighty person a bit of a nutter.
explanation.definitionFit: A social flitter who never settles is likened to the insect, and a wing nut with two flat lugs bears the same name.

clue.text: It's appropriate among those living monastic life

explanation.surface: A remark that something is fitting for monks.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means proper or permissible, and literally places someone within a religious brotherhood.

clue.text: Cake prepared at length by a German girl

parts.note: prepared means made
eine is the German word for 'a' used with a feminine noun, so a German 'a' that is girlish

explanation.surface: A cake baked to great length by a German girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a German girl' is not a person: EINE is the feminine form of the German indefinite article; 'at' and 'by' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A madeleine is a small shell-shaped French sponge cake.

clue.text: Financial experts, most in tears when ruined

indicators.note: ruined says the words most in tears are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Economists left mostly in tears after a financial ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: Monetarists are economists who hold that controlling the money supply governs the economy.

clue.text: Plant growing wild in north

indicators.note: growing wild suggests the letters of north run riot and rearrange

explanation.surface: A plant that grows wild up north.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorn is a prickly bush such as hawthorn, so it names a plant.

clue.text: Main supply of fuel

parts.note: read as the principal source of energy, but 'main' is the sea, so fuel supplied from beneath the sea off Britain's east coast

explanation.surface: A phrase about the chief source of fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' means the open sea; this is natural gas piped from fields beneath the sea between Britain and Scandinavia.
explanation.definitionFit: This fuel comes from undersea fields and fed most of Britain's mains supply.

clue.text: 7 bovine creatures

explanation.surface: A reference to another clue, then some cattle.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 points to 7-down, meaning tidy or orderly; neat is also an old word for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat means tidy and well arranged, and in older English it is a collective word for oxen and cows.

clue.text: Ted Heath for one forbade German songs to be heard

indicators.note: to be heard says the phrase is spoken and its sound gives the answer

parts.note: forbade is banned and German songs are Lieder, the German art songs

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister Ted Heath banned German songs from being played.
explanation.walkthrough: Ted Heath here is not the British Prime Minister Edward Heath but the swing-era band leader of the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ted Heath led a famous British big band in the 1940s and 50s, an example of a conductor of a dance band.

clue.text: I reacted stupidly in fast-moving current

indicators.note: stupidly says the letters of I reacted are jumbled foolishly

explanation.surface: Confessing to a foolish reaction while caught in a strong current.
explanation.definitionFit: A tidal race is a fast, turbulent stretch of water caused by the tide.

clue.text: Again offer to explain

explanation.surface: An instruction to resubmit something and give an explanation.
explanation.definitionFit: To present again is to re-offer, and to depict or state a case is to describe or set it out.

clue.text: Ahead, but not among the medal winners, we're informed

indicators.note: we're informed says we only hear this, so the sound counts

parts.note: the place after gold, silver and bronze misses out on a medal

explanation.surface: Being told an athlete led but just missed the podium.
explanation.walkthrough: The place just outside the medals sounds the same as a word meaning onward.
explanation.definitionFit: Forth means forwards or onward, as in 'go forth'.

clue.text: Everyone given the sack? That's excessive

explanation.surface: Mass redundancy complained about as going too far.
explanation.definitionFit: Every worker dismissed, and the American informal intensifier meaning extreme or tremendous.

clue.text: Summarise main points concerning limit placed on spending

parts.note: re means concerning, as in business letters
a cap is an upper limit, such as a spending cap

explanation.surface: A summary of the key points about a budget ceiling.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for recapitulate, it means go over the main points again.

clue.text: Are rich characters possibly more wary?

indicators.note: characters possibly says the letters of are rich may be rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking whether wealthy people are more cautious.
explanation.definitionFit: Charier is the comparative of chary, meaning cautious.

clue.text: This sword is mine

explanation.surface: Someone claiming ownership of a sword.
explanation.definitionFit: The great Scottish broadsword shares its name with an American directional anti-personnel explosive device laid in the ground.

clue.text: Positions junk in store

indicators.note: junk, as a verb meaning to scrap, says the words in store are broken up

explanation.surface: Positions of old rubbish kept in a storeroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Orients means aligns or positions something in relation to its surroundings.

clue.text: North of border, a navy battle

indicators.note: in a down answer north means above, so the navy piece sits over the border piece

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy
a hem is the border of a garment

explanation.surface: A naval battle fought just north of the frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'North of' means written above, so the navy abbreviation stands on top of the garment edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Arnhem was the site of the 1944 Allied airborne battle in the Netherlands.

clue.text: Political skill needed after tact's failed

indicators.note: failed says the letters of after tact's have collapsed and are reordered

parts.note: the possessive s is used as a letter here

explanation.surface: Diplomatic skill is required once tact has failed.
explanation.definitionFit: Statecraft is the art of conducting government affairs.

clue.text: Amazingly stores such energy

indicators.note: stores says the word Amazingly holds the answer within it

explanation.surface: A claim that something amazingly holds such energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Zing is lively energy or zest.

clue.text: Family clash brought to early close

indicators.note: brought to early close means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a clang is a loud clash of metal

explanation.surface: A family row cut short early.
explanation.walkthrough: The clash is the noise, not a quarrel; 'brought to early close' drops its final G.
explanation.definitionFit: A clan is an extended family group, especially in Scotland.

clue.text: Hit small child

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a mite is a small child

explanation.surface: An order to strike a little child.
explanation.definitionFit: Smite is an old word for strike hard.

clue.text: Something problematic for actor, bringing bad luck!

explanation.surface: A difficult script proves unlucky for a performer.
explanation.definitionFit: Difficult speeches to learn in a play, and a British exclamation of sympathy meaning tough luck.

clue.text: Mechanical procedure accepted by Prime Minister for the time being

indicators.note: accepted by means taken inside the Prime Minister's letters

parts.note: rote is mechanical routine repetition

explanation.surface: A routine procedure approved by the Prime Minister as a stopgap.
explanation.definitionFit: Pro tem is short for the Latin pro tempore, meaning temporarily.

clue.text: Foreign martial arts expert is hard

parts.note: a dan is a grade of expertise in judo or karate, or a holder of it
taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A tough fighter from overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: Danish (from Denmark) stands loosely for foreign from a British point of view.
explanation.definitionFit: Being from Denmark makes someone or something non-British, hence from abroad.
